Khopesh

ḫpš

Origin
Egypt
Period
Bronze Age, widely used c. 1550 to 1070 BC
Blade
45 cm
Weight
Under 1 kg
Edge
Single, on the outer curve
Grip
One-handed

The khopesh is a sickle-shaped bronze sword. Its curved outer edge cut, and the hooked end could catch a shield or a limb.

Egyptian armies used it in the New Kingdom, and pharaohs are shown holding it in carved reliefs. After the Bronze Age it gave way to straight iron swords.
